claim: OU leads analysis of the "CHROMA-D" detector

suggestion.to: The OU is developing a combined visible-infrared imager, with a detector made by Teledyne e2v, for future Mars missions such as I-MIM and ESA’s LightShip-1. It can tell water ice from carbon dioxide ice on the surface. In December 2025 the UK Space Agency awarded the OU £1.2 million for the next phase.
